title: A2A & MCP Workshop: Automating Business Processes with LLMs — Damien Murphy, Bench
talk_summary: A workshop demo of a host A2A orchestrator delegating to Slack/GitHub/research sub-agents over MCP (via Zapier), with substantial Q&A on context management, prompt caching, and model routing.

takeaways.technique: Sub-agent context isolation (protect host prompt from tool/raw data)
takeaways.what_they_do: Host agent sends only a small task to a sub-agent; the sub-agent absorbs the large tool results/raw data and returns only the business-value summary, so the host context grows only incrementally.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the host agent only processes the summaries. Um, and the raw data is discarded after processing.

takeaways.what_they_do: They measured tool definitions alone consuming ~10k tokens and one added MCP server adding 11k more; they hide MCP servers behind sub-agents so tool schemas don't bloat the primary prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I think we're up to like you know 10,000 tokens just for tool definitions alone. Um, I added the Asana MCP. It added 11,000 more tokens
takeaways.numbers: ~10k tokens for tool defs; +11k from one MCP server

takeaways.what_they_do: They simulated cache-marker strategies (linear/exponential/fixed growth) against usage data, noting cache writes cost ~3x a normal request and that caching the last turn of single-turn sessions is wasteful.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the cost to actually push that into the cache uh is about threex the cost of of making a single request
takeaways.numbers: 25-35% cost savings across strategies; ~30k tokens optimal cache point

takeaways.technique: Cheap router LLM in front of expensive agents
takeaways.what_they_do: They route tasks by depth: Gemini Flash for summarization, Claude Sonnet for tool calling, and a routing LLM decides how deep/expensive a task needs to go rather than defaulting to Opus.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need uh intelligent rooting logic on like does this task need the entire context right does it need 20,000 tokens
takeaways.numbers: Opus ~5% better than Sonnet but ~4x cost

takeaways.what_they_do: They model sub-agent work as a directed acyclic graph (parallel fan-out, then fan-in) analogous to CI/CD pipelines, with max-turn caps to stop recursion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're looking at uh directed a cyclic grass right so dags um as a part of of bench sub agent tasks

takeaways.technique: Synthetic demo accounts + fake-customer agents for tool testing
takeaways.what_they_do: They test write-actions against demo Salesforce/Slack accounts with synthetic data, using bot agents to post fake conversations and a support bot to respond, rather than mocking every tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have a few agents that actually will go in and and just post like conversations ... and then we can we can just test uh on synthetic data
